name: Speed of light, astronomical unit, light-year, parsec (SI/IAU defined values)

source.located: c: the SI defining constant (1983 metre redefinition, retained in the 2019 SI), READ as restated in CODATA 2022, Mohr-Newell-Taylor-Tiesinga, arXiv:2409.03787v1, Table XXXII p.50 ('speed of light in vacuum c 299 792 458 m s^-1 exact') and p.60 ('already exactly known as a result of the 1983 redefinition of the meter in terms of an exact value of c and the 2019 revision of the SI'). au: IAU 2012 Resolution B2, READ as restated in Prsa et al., 'Nominal values for selected solar and planetary quantities: IAU 2015 Resolution B3', arXiv:1605.09788v1 (31 May 2016) p.8 ('In 2012, the IAU passed a resolution that defines the astronomical unit as 149 597 870 700 m') and p.13 note 2 ('Resolution B2 of the 2012 IAU General Assembly adopted an exact value for the astronomical unit'), and in arXiv:1510.07674v1 endnote 4 ('defined the astronomical unit to be a conventional unit of length equal to 149 597 870 700 m exactly'). pc: IAU 2015 Resolution B2 (notes), READ as restated in arXiv:1605.09788v1 p.8 ('IAU 2015 Resolution B2 adopted the definition of the parsec to be exactly 648000/pi au ... Since pi is irrational, the length of one parsec cannot be rational, but it still is an exact number, 3.085 677 581 491... x 10^16 m') and p.13 note 2 ('1 pc = 648000 pi^-1 au'). ly: c x Julian year (365.25 d x 86400 s): the IAU/Julian-year definition was NOT read at any source here (NAMED-NOT-READ); the value is COMPUTED from the read c and the stated Julian-year hypothesis.

published_statement: (i) c = 299 792 458 m s^-1, exact, a defining constant of the SI (CODATA 2022 Table XXXII p.50; p.60). (ii) 'Resolution B2 of the XXVIII General Assembly of the IAU in 2012 defined the astronomical unit to be a conventional unit of length equal to 149 597 870 700 m exactly' (1510.07674 endnote 4; 1605.09788 p.8, p.13). (iii) 'IAU 2015 Resolution B2 adopted the definition of the parsec to be exactly 648000/pi au ... it still is an exact number, 3.085 677 581 491... x 10^16 m' (1605.09788 p.8); '1 pc = 648000 pi^-1 au' (p.13 note 2). (iv) light-year: no published statement READ here; the tree's hypothesis LY = c x Julian year is computed: 9 460 730 472 580 800 m exactly.
published_hypotheses: H1 (c): the SI is in force (metre defined through a fixed numerical value of c); c carries zero uncertainty by construction -- a convention, not a measurement.
H2 (au): the au is a CONVENTIONAL (nominal) unit of length fixed at 149 597 870 700 m (IAU 2012 B2) -- not the measured Earth-Sun mean distance and not tied to the Gaussian gravitational constant.
H3 (pc): the parsec is defined from the au by the exact factor 648000/pi (IAU 2015 B2 notes); it is exact but irrational in metres.
H4 (ly, NOT READ at source): the light-year is the distance light travels in vacuum in one Julian year of 365.25 days of 86400 SI seconds.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis does not bite on this result, and the evidence is structural rather than presumed. Three of the four values are CONVENTIONS, not measurements: c has been fixed since 1983 (CODATA 2022 p.60), the au since 2012 as 'a conventional unit of length ... exactly' (1510.07674 endnote 4), the parsec since 2015 as exactly 648000/pi au (1605.09788 p.8). A defined unit cannot be wrong for lack of data -- no future measurement can move it; new data can only change what the unit is USED to express (e.g. the physical Earth-Sun distance, which the conventional au by definition no longer tracks). The fourth, the light-year, is c times a conventional year; the only open choice is WHICH year (a hypothesis, not a datum), and it moves one printed row at the 4th significant figure (8.42 -> 8.43 ly, R7). Before 2012 the au WAS a measured/derived quantity (Gaussian-constant based); what data earlier astronomers lacked there is outside this audit's reach -- the pre-2012 IAU 1976/2009 systems are NAMED-NOT-READ here -- and it is irrelevant to the tree, which uses the post-2012 defined value. Evidence either way: every tree literal equals the defined value exactly (c, au) or to 11 s.f. (ly, pc), and no output changes (R1-R6). The one discrepancy found (the prose 810 AU / 2.6 ly against the code's 2002 AU / 0.084 ly, R8) is internal to the tree and is shown NOT to be explicable by any value of the constants.
grade_evidence: Statement READ-VIA-RESTATEMENT (CODATA 2022 for c; IAU 2015 B3 papers 1605.09788/1510.07674 restating IAU 2012 B2 for au and IAU 2015 B2 for pc); the light-year definition is NAMED-NOT-READ but the tree's own stated form (Julian year x c) is computed exactly. Re-derivation in exact sympy arithmetic: c and AU literals identical to the defined values; LY and PC literals are the exact values rounded to 11 s.f. (rel 2.0e-12, 2.8e-12); PC feeds no output; every printed AU and ly figure in arrival.py is unchanged under exact constants, and c cancels identically from the magsail floor. No datum has moved (all four are defined). Hypothesis drifts are labels ('exact' for two rounded literals; 'IAU 2012' for a 2015 parsec definition; 'SI' for a non-SI unit) that change no value. Not NARROWED: the tree uses these constants on exactly the class they are defined for (unit conversion). Separately recorded, NOT part of this grade and NOT an error in the constants: the owner's prose figures '810 AU' (arrival.py:151,159; launcher.py:180,291; index3.py:86) and '2.6 ly' (arrival.py:152) disagree with the owner's own printed output (2001.64 AU, 0.0842 ly) by factors 2.47 and 30.9 that no admissible au/ly reconciles (R8) -- a discrepancy for the owner of the magsail result, to be READ before it is quoted.
what_would_change_the_grade: (a) A reading of the IAU/Julian-year light-year definition showing a year other than 365.25 d x 86400 s would make the 100 km row's printed 8.42 ly a 4th-figure discrepancy (it becomes 8.43 under Gregorian/tropical years, R7) -- still not a change to any conclusion. (b) A future IAU/CGPM redefinition of the au, parsec or c (none found; the later-literature search could not be run -- quota) would make the grade DATA-DEPENDENT. (c) A reading of IAU 2012 B2 / IAU 2015 B2 at source contradicting the restatements in 1605.09788 would reopen H2/H3. Nothing currently in hand moves it.
